# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability or an exposed secret

Please **don't open a public issue** for security problems.

Use GitHub's private reporting instead: go to the **Security** tab of this repository and choose **Report a vulnerability**. Include what you found, where, and how to reproduce it. Don't include real credentials in the report.

This is a personal project maintained on a best-effort basis, so I can't promise a response time or a fix date, but I will look at every report.

## If you find a credential in this repository

Treat it as compromised. Report it privately as described above, and if it belongs to you, revoke or rotate it right away. Removing it from a later commit doesn't remove it from git history.

## Supported versions

Only the latest commit of each maintained branch is considered. Older tags and versions don't get fixes.
